# New Guidelines for Responsible Use of Generative AI (GenAI)
JHU and IT@JH leadership recently released a set of**guidelines for the responsible use of GenAI**. These guidelines were established to ensure that GenAI technologies are used safely and in compliance with current policies and include the following:
* Start with our approved GenAI tools andconnect with IT@JHbefore procuring new ones
* Do not enter proprietary dataâincluding clinical, financial, or business recordsâinto third-party, unapproved GenAI tools
* You are responsible for any AI-generated content that you produce or publish
* Adhere to current university policies
Over the next few months IT@JH will be deploying new tools and resources âincluding our own AI platform, the âHopkins AI Lab.â Invitations to join the Hopkins AI Lab will be rolling out over the next few months, but thesupport siteis available now. OurAI resourcesare also expanding. Stay tuned for more exciting updates on how IT@JH is working to advance the use of GenAI across Johns Hopkins.

# Generative AI: What Faculty Need to Know

- by kbennett
- May 7, 2026May 7, 2026
- Administration

As you may have read in the JHU announcement dated December 11, 2025, Johns Hopkins has launched HopGPT, a secure, Hopkinsâdeveloped generative AI platform available free of charge to all JHU and JHM faculty, staff, and students. HopGPT provides JHEDâauthenticated access to multiple large language models (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Llama) in a privacyâprotective environment appropriate for institutional and sensitive data.

### Department of Medicine Guidance

Consistent with University guidance, the DOM does not expect faculty to individually pay for commercially available âbaseâ AI tools (e.g., standard ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions) when comparable functionality is already available through HopGPT at no cost. As such, reimbursement or grant charging for basic LLM subscriptions (e.g., ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro) is generally not supported when HopGPT meets the need.

The DOM recognizes that some faculty are building or extending AI tools for research or educational innovation. In these cases, faculty may need capabilities not currently available within HopGPT, such as:

- API access, tokens, or usage credits
- Custom AI development or testing
- Grantâfunded or instructional AI applications

Given this distinction, DOM members are encouraged to explore HopGPT, review the GenAI resources and training materials available through IT@JH, and reach out to DOMFINANCE@jh.edu if they have questions about appropriate AI use or reimbursement pathways

### Looking Ahead

HopGPTâand the broader ecosystem of AI tools at Johns Hopkinsâwill continue to evolve. As Hopkins expands functionality, we expect that guidance on approved and discouraged tools will be updated, with an emphasis on helping faculty innovate while maintaining institutional standards for security, compliance, and stewardship.
